newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian police hold Australian businessman.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian police hold Australian businessman.

text.p: Cambodian police said on Saturday that they had detained the president of the Australian Business Association of Cambodia after one of the businessman's creditors accused him of theft.

John Harper, who runs a food import and distribution business and a popular restaurant in Phnom Penh, was taken into custody on Friday, said Simon Parr, one of Harper's partners in United Distributors Cambodia.
Police said they did not know whether Harper was, or will be charged as the courts were closed for the weekend.
Parr said the firm was trying to secure his release but that the weekend closures were hindering their efforts.
"There was a restaurant that owed an amount of money and closed down. It appeared to us that we'd never get our money back," said Parr.
He said Harper was "invited to a house" to collect goods as security against the debt and added that the matter had since been taken before a judge.
Harper had cooperated with authorities but was detained after accompanying police to a central Phnom Penh police station, Parr said.
"The police have put it down that we broke in (to the house), which was incorrect," Parr said.
